il, NON MENTIOR {m}, & les autres autheurs ſoyent
auſsi gens de literature grãde, & recõmẽdable foy: tou-
tesfois leur authorité n'eſt pas neceſſaire, ni ſi venerable
que le lecteur ſoit obligé les croire {n}. Et quant à Salomõ
& Achaz, beaucoup d'eſcriuains biẽ doctes, fõt autremẽt
le cõte de leurs ans.'Tant y a, que quand biẽ cela ſeroit
ainſi, ce ſont des exẽples beaux, certes, & memorables:
mais ſi rares pourtãt, que nous ne deuons, ne pouuõs les
tirer à conſequence {o}. Et nos loix en ce faict, comme en
tous autres, s'arreſtẽt aux cas & negoces qu'elles voyent
ou penſent le plus ſouuent aduenir {p}. Voire meſmes, ce
grand oracle de Philoſophie, Plato, parlant de l'aage con
uenable aux hõmes & femmes, pour ſe marier, ordõnoit
aux hommes le trentieme an, iuſqu'au trentecinq: & aux
fẽmes, du ſeizieme, iuſqu'au vingtieme {q}, & Ariſtote ſon

ont trop plus prudemmẽt, ce me ſemble, preueu & conſi-
deré que pluſieurs ſont ſi mal naiz, & d'vne cõcupiſcence

margin_notes.beside_line: en là premiere ieuneſſe-deſquels, le deſir de la chair bouil

uncertain.text: en là premiere ieuneſſe-deſquels, le deſir de la chair bouil
uncertain.note: the a of 'la' carries a distinct detached wedge accent, the same shape and weight as the grave on 'à peine' in line 3 of this page, while the plain a of 'de la chair' later in the same line has none. Transcribed as printed ('là', sic); the sense wants the article 'la'.

uncertain.text: en là premiere ieuneſſe-deſquels, le deſir de la chair bouil
uncertain.note: a short mid-height wedge stands between 'ieuneſſe' and 'deſquels', the same mark this page uses for a line-end word break ('tou-', line 15). Read as a hyphen inside the line (§2); it could also be an ink speck in a tight setting.

uncertain.text: (qui le faiſoit coucher auec elle) la cognut en fin, & rẽdit
uncertain.note: the mark over the e of 'rẽdit' is a broad, flat, slightly wavy bar, unlike the short steep acute of 'irrité' one line above: read as a tilde (rẽdit = rendit).

uncertain.text: ſieurs attribuẽt à Salomõ, & Achaz Rois, leſquels (ſelon
uncertain.note: same judgement as line 5: the mark over the e of 'attribuẽt' is a long flat bar, not the short steep grave printed on the following 'à'. Read as a tilde (attribuent).

uncertain.note: 'eut' and 'Ezechiel' are set with no space at all (the t and the E touch); transcribed as printed per §1. The marker is the italic l of the margin fount.

uncertain.note: DOMINO TESTE (line 13) and NON MENTIOR (line 14) are set in widely letterspaced capitals; closed up per §3 and the block carries spaced_caps. The closing parenthesis is set tight against the D; spaced per §1.

uncertain.text: auſsi gens de literature grãde, & recõmẽdable foy: tou-
uncertain.note: the word-break sign after 'tou' is a small worn wedge sitting near the baseline rather than a clean hyphen; transcribed as '-' per §1. It could be mistaken for a full stop.

uncertain.text: le cõte de leurs ans.'Tant y a, que quand biẽ cela ſeroit
uncertain.note: a well-inked raised comma stands between 'ans.' and 'Tant', the size and weight of type rather than a speck. Transcribed as an apostrophe; its purpose is unclear.

uncertain.text: en l'an quatorzieme, à l'hõme: & au douzieme, à là fem-
uncertain.note: second occurrence of an accented article on this page: the a of 'la' carries a grave-shaped stroke. Transcribed as printed ('là', sic).

a small light mark sits above the a of 'la' at the very edge of the margin column. It is fainter and smaller than the clear tildes in this margin (e.g. 'trimoniũ', 'cõſ.'), and 'en la ſomme' needs none; read as 'la'.
'me' (the continuation of 'Hiero-me') and 'en' are set with no space between them; transcribed as printed per §1.
'ad' and 'Vi' are set with no space; the line-end break sign is the worn wedge used elsewhere on this page and is transcribed as '-'.

the key letter of this note is printed as the italic k of the margin fount (an l-shaped stem followed by a z-like leg, easily misread as 'lz'); it matches the body marker after 'des enfans' and follows i in the printer's alphabet, so the key is 'k'. The first line is read 'Io. And.' (Ioannes Andreae).
a raised comma/apostrophe, fully inked and the size of type, stands between 'Panor.' and 'au'. Kept as an apostrophe; it may be an abbreviation mark or a stray sort.
the last letter is a round e, not the crossed italic t of 'Vitalem' on the next line; transcribed as printed ('eſcriuane', sic, for 'eſcriuant').
the letter before the stop is read as the æ ligature (à præ[lato]); at this size it could be a plain a.
'ego' and 'ſolis' are set with no space between them; transcribed as printed per §1.
the last letter before the stop has a tall ascender crossed at x-height: the italic t of this fount, not the short italic r. Read 'Paragt.'; 'Paragr.' is the obvious alternative.

the foot line begins with an unkeyed word 'loix.', which is the end of margin note key q ('Republique, & au vi. des' / 'loix.'): the margin ran out of room at the foot of the column. Recorded as an unkeyed foot entry rather than a second note with key q.
the signature is printed 'A ij.' with a full stop; a small detached speck sits to the left of the A and is ignored. No catchword is printed.
